runtime/browser-surface/run-coordinator..reason: 2026-07-31 (orphan-capacity reconcile, live evidence: pdpp-neko-amazon-dd6ffc79c80ddfd3/bs_4f3d919a and pdpp-neko-amazon-83b5b114cb3b7f72/bs_1ec177c0 stayed running+Docker-healthy and capacity-consuming after every sweep tick while their durable browser_surfaces rows sat at health=unhealthy, no lease, last_used_at ~23:51). Root cause: reconcileSurfacesWithAllocator's own eviction branch (live.health === unhealthy -> invalidateSurface) removes a wedged surface from the lease manager's in-memory map and persists it unhealthy, but invalidateSurface never calls allocator.stopSurface -- and cleanupIdleSurfaces only ever considers surfaces still present in the manager's map at health ready. Once a surface reaches persisted unhealthy with no lease, nothing in this file or in @opendatalabs/remote-surface ever calls stopSurface for it again, so its allocator container and host-port capacity slot leak forever -- distinct from, and does not touch, the reconcileSurfacesWithAllocator/cleanupIdleSurfaces upstream-fix path from the prior same-day stale-capacity incident. Fix: retireOrphanedUnhealthyBrowserSurfaces, composed into the existing periodic sweep after cleanupIdleBrowserSurfaces, reads the durable store directly (the manager has already forgotten these rows) for health=unhealthy + no active lease + not retained + aged past idleTtlMs, then retireOrphanedUnhealthyBrowserSurface issues one bounded allocator.stopSurface(reason: reconcile) per candidate after re-checking the manager still agrees no non-terminal lease owns it. A live deployment can accumulate hundreds of historical unhealthy/no-lease rows (see MAX_ORPHAN_SURFACE_RETIREMENTS_PER_SWEEP), so the eligible set is sorted deterministically (oldest last_used_at first, surface_id tiebreaker) and sliced to a small per-tick batch rather than firing an unbounded burst of allocator calls every sweep interval; each retired row leaves the eligibility set (health -> stopping) whether stopSurface succeeds or reports the container already gone, so the batch converges across a few ticks with no separate retry bookkeeping, and one candidate's transient stopSurface failure leaves only that row untouched (naturally retried next tick) without blocking the rest of the batch. Net mass increase (83->92, +9, re-derived via measure-mass.ts --files): two new functions (retireOrphanedUnhealthyBrowserSurfaces, the per-item retireOrphanedUnhealthyBrowserSurface) plus one new injectable clock dep field (nowMs) threaded through the factory destructure and wired at the one call site in sweepBrowserSurfaceLeases, after cleanupIdleBrowserSurfaces. All prior mass (idle cleanup, boot reconcile, expiry/reclaim) is untouched -- confirmed via git diff showing zero changes to cleanupIdleBrowserSurfaces or reconcileBrowserSurfacesWithAllocatorAtBoot themselves. || 2026-07-31 (bounded mid-run phase-scoped surface acquire/release): adds the phase lifecycle a `surfaceScope: "phase"` connector needs so it stops reserving a scarce managed surface for its whole run (Slack: ~1h of archive/backfill to cover four quick gap streams). Net 92->106 (+14, re-derived via measure-mass.ts --files) across four small functions, each individually UNDER Biome's cognitive-complexity threshold (biome lint --only=complexity/noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity reports zero diagnostics for this file): (1) acquireManagedBrowserSurfaceForPhase, whose branches are the contract itself -- not-managed short-circuit, idempotent-reuse arm, and the `waiting_for_browser_surface` interception that cancels the just-queued wait so a phase request NEVER blocks its run on capacity; (2) releaseManagedBrowserSurfaceForPhase, whose branches are the ownership fence (delete-record-before-release so a duplicate/concurrent call cannot double-release, and release under the RECORDED fencing token so a stale call cannot free a newer grant); (3) grantFromPhaseLease, whose guard exists only to satisfy noUncheckedIndexedAccess without a non-null assertion; (4) phaseUnavailableReasonForEarlyReturn, a 2-branch status mapping. Reduction was attempted and measured, not assumed: extracting the nested idempotent-reuse block into `reusablePhaseGrant` lowered the file 111->106 and was kept. Further extraction was rejected as clean-code theater -- it would split one lifecycle contract across more shallow helpers without removing a single state distinction, and every remaining branch is a correctness guard (no double-release, no leak, no unbounded wait, no capacity bypass) rather than incidental structure. Also fixes a proven defect in the same file: reconcileBrowserSurfaceLeasesAfterBoot built activeRunIds from persisted run_ids only, and reconcileAfterRestart (@opendatalabs/remote-surface surface-lease-manager.js:553-560) releases any leased lease whose run_id is absent from that set -- so a controller restart mid-phase silently released a surface still in use; the derived phase session id is now included per active run.

server/connector-summary-terminal-publis.reason: New file (2026-07-31, fleet-summary-terminal-publisher): the one bounded maintenance authority that assembles a ConnectorListSummaryTerminalProjection for a swept page of connections and calls the already-fenced publishConnectorListSummaryTerminalProjection. publishConnectorListSummaryTerminalProjection/getConnectorListSummaryTerminalProjection[Batch] have existed since the terminal-gate revision, fully CAS-fenced and unit-tested, but had zero production callsites -- list_summary_projection_* sat permanently stale/unobserved. Scoped-ingest-outcome-summary fix (2026-07-30, +4): listSourceInstanceHeartbeatsByConnectionIds' LEFT JOIN subquery aggregated MAX(accepted_at) GROUP BY device_id, source_instance_id over the entire device_ingest_batch_outcomes table (filtered only by status='accepted'), so the connector-summary LIST read's cost grew with total fleet-wide ingest history instead of the requested page. The predicate is deliberately derived through device_source_instances rather than filtering device_ingest_batch_outcomes.connector_instance_id directly: legacy rows written through recordBatchOutcome's insert-batch-outcome path can carry an empty-string connector_instance_id (normalizeOutcome's `?? ""` default), so filtering the aggregate by that column would silently drop real ingest history for those rows. Proven by N=0/1/25 SQLite tests asserting exact parity against the unscoped legacy aggregate, no off-page leakage from a larger unrelated fleet fixture, and an EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN assertion that the subquery does not fall back to scanning all of device_ingest_batch_outcomes. fix-fleet-local-collector-evidence-completeness independent-gate follow-up (2026-07-31, +8, both backends): replaces the two-step (revoke-before-consume) supersedePriorDevicesForBinding with consumeEnrollmentCodeAndSupersedePriorDevices, which folds the enrollment-code consume UPDATE and the prior-device revoke cascade into ONE transaction so a losing/failed replacement enrollment can never revoke the device it was trying to replace (the independent gate's blocking finding #1). Tried collapsing the two guard checks into one compound condition; measured no mass reduction (the two conditions gate genuinely independent decisions — race outcome vs. adopted-vs-new — and Biome's cognitive-complexity scoring counts them identically either way). Proven load-bearing by a path-bound regression (device-exporter-routes.test.ts, "a replacement enrollment that fails before completion never revokes the prior working device") verified failing against the pre-fix two-step code (reverted to e43348b17's content, confirmed actual: 'revoked') and passing after.
